In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them. He said Modi thought foreign leaders were his friends, and “they caught him”. He said India squandered a great opportunity presented by the Iran war to play the mediator, and the role was usurped by Pakistan.In what had the large audience from across the country in splits, Rahul illustrated Modi’s hugging by giving a bear hug to Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit - who in turn asked Rahul jokingly “if he had thought he was hugging Italian PM Meloni”, and by enacting other practical jokes. He also cited a childhood anecdote of how then PM Indira Gandhi did not take seriously the US administration’s attempt to flatter her via the then First Lady.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said ‘we’ will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
Article Summary: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova. According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft. A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site.

Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: Reservation Hatao Andolan: Over 50 detained at Jantar Mantar; reservation should go to poor, not castes: Protesters
Article Text:
More than 50 protesters who had gathered at Jantar Mantar were detained by Delhi Police on Friday.

Reservation should go to poor, not castes: Protesters





NEW DELHI: More than 50 protesters who had gathered at Jantar Mantar demanding changes to India’s reservation system were detained by cops Friday.While hundreds had gathered through the day, the situation escalated around 7.30pm as several protesters who remained at the spot beyond the prescribed time of 4pm began raising slogans. This prompted the deployment of additional Delhi Police personnel and Rapid Action Force.Police said most protesters had left after the demonstration ended, but several remained at the spot despite repeated requests to disperse. The situation was later brought under control and Jantar Mantar was cleared.By afternoon, demonstrators had assembled at Jantar Mantar behind police barricades, carrying placards and raising slogans such as “Aarakshan gareeb ko mile, jaati ko nahi” (reservation should go to the poor, not castes). The demonstration, organised under the banner of the social media-driven ‘Reservation Hatao Andolan’, also saw protesters calling for a rollback of the UGC roster system.At the centre of the protest was the demand to replace caste-based reservation with a system based on economic criteria. Protesters drew comparisons between students or families in similar economic circumstances but belonging to different castes, questioning why their access to educational institutions, govt jobs, scholarships and welfare schemes should differ.“We study in the same school, sit in the same classroom and are taught by the same teacher. Then why should I face rejection even after scoring 85%, while someone else gets selected with 45%?” questioned protester Abhinav Rai.Protesters also advocated a “one family, one reservation, one time” policy, arguing that reservation benefits should not continue across generations within the same family once a member has availed of them. They sought a rollback of the UGC roster system and the introduction of a time limit, or “sunset clause”, for reservation. Some called for caste identity to be removed from public life, raising the slogan “one nation, one identity”.UPSC aspirant Aniket Kumar said reservation policies should be periodically reviewed rather than continue indefinitely in their present form. “The idea is that reservation benefits should not continue across generations within the same family once a member has already benefited from them,” he said.The protesters also raised concerns over differences in age limits and the number of attempts available to candidates in govt recruitment examinations, including UPSC, SSC, railway and banking exams. They argued that relaxations available to some categories effectively give candidates a longer window to compete, while general-category aspirants face tighter age and attempt limits.Police at the venue said up to 500 people had been permitted to demonstrate until 4pm, with no permission granted for an overnight sit-in. Barricades were erected around the protest site to keep the gathering confined to the designated area.The demonstration affected traffic in and around central Delhi. Sansad Marg was restricted, while diversions and restrictions were put in place on Tolstoy Road and Ashoka Road. The curbs increased traffic pressure on surrounding stretches, with congestion reported on KG Marg near Connaught Place, Barakhamba Road and Janpath Road.Traffic sources said personnel were deployed at key points to regulate vehicle movement and enforce the restrictions. “The deployment is also there from local police and everyone is acting on their directions,” a traffic source said.Sources, however, said the congestion could not be attributed solely to the Jantar Mantar demonstration, as another protest was taking place near Parliament Street police station, adding to traffic pressure around Sansad Marg.
Article Summary: More than 50 protesters who had gathered at Jantar Mantar were detained by Delhi Police on Friday. At the centre of the protest was the demand to replace caste- based reservation with a system based on economic criteria. Protesters drew comparisons between students or families in similar economic circumstances but belonging to different castes.

Article Title: Shahdara flyover repairs to continue till Aug 31, traffic likely to slow
Article Text:
New Delhi:





Commuters using the Shahdara flyover towards Apsara Border will have to brace for slower traffic as renovation and repair work on the stretch is expected to continue till Aug 31, Delhi Traffic Police said in an advisory.The location is a crucial commuter corridor for people travelling between east Delhi and the Apsara Border towards Ghaziabad , with the stretch witnessing heavy movement during morning and evening peak hours.The traffic police have advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance and factor in additional travel time. The traffic police said adequate personnel have been deployed at the location for traffic regulation and facilitation.
Article Summary: Commuters using the Shahdara flyover towards Apsara Border will have to brace for slower traffic as renovation and repair work on the stretch is expected to continue till Aug 31. The traffic police have advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance and factor in additional travel time. The location is a crucial commuter corridor for people travelling between east Delhi and the Aapsara Border towards Ghaziabad.

Article Title: Labourer killed, 3 injured as Karol Bagh building collapses during demolition
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A labourer died and three others suffered injuries after an old multistorey building collapsed during demolition work in central Delhi’s Karol Bagh Friday morning.The incident occurred around 11.15 am at a property on Pyare Lal Road in Regarpura. The building was being demolished by a private contractor engaged by its owners. A preliminary inquiry found that permission for the demolition had not been obtained from the agency concerned.Police said labourers were working at the site when the structure collapsed, trapping workers under the debris. Following an alert, police personnel and Delhi Fire Services teams reached the spot and launched a rescue operation.Among the affected labourers, Sheikh Shamshad suffered severe injuries and later died. His body has been shifted to a hospital mortuary for post-mortem examination, said police.Another worker, Mohammad Ayub, suffered a head injury and a fracture in his right hand. He was rescued from the debris and taken to a hospital. Police said his condition is critical.A third labourer, Sheikh Saidul, suffered injuries to his limbs and is undergoing treatment.A fourth worker, Rafik Ul, suffered minor injuries and returned home after treatment.Investigators have detained the building owners and the contractor for questioning. They are examining the circumstances under which the demolition work was undertaken and whether mandatory permissions and safety measures were in place.Delhi Fire Services said portions of the upper floors collapsed during the demolition work, injuring the labourers. Officials said legal action would be initiated after verification of facts and assessment of the circumstances that led to the collapse.In a statement, MCD said it received a complaint from the Karol Bagh zonal control room about the collapse of a portion of a building at 3512/6, Pyare Lal Road. The civic body said its field staff reached the site within 10 minutes and found that the owners were carrying out the demolition themselves. Barricades made of GI sheets had been installed around the building.According to MCD, the incident occurred while labourers were engaged in the demolition work.An MCD official said the building was around 100 years old and was being demolished, a process that usually does not require permission. “During the inspection, it was found that a wall had collapsed, leading to the accident,” the official said.
Article Summary: A labourer died and three others suffered injuries after an old multistorey building collapsed during demolition work. The incident occurred around 11.15 am at a property on Pyare Lal Road in Regarpura. The building was being demolished by a private contractor engaged by its owners.

Article Title: Despite 23000 cases for unauthorised travel last year, disabled passengers face struggles in Divyangjan coaches
Article Text: MUMBAI: Thursday’s incident where a disabled commuter was pushed off a moving local train and killed by an able-bodied commuter following an argument over seats should be a “wake-up call” for the Railways, said activists, demanding sustained action against unauthorised travel in Divyangjan (handicapped) coaches.In 2025, the Railway Protection Force (RPF) registered over 23,000 cases of unauthorised travel on Western and Central Railway put together. But disabled commuters continue to grapple with challenges while boarding and alighting from Divyangjan coaches that are packed with able-bodied passengers in peak hours.“Altercations in Divyangjan coaches are a common feature during peak hours. Disabled commuters frequently face abuse, are prevented from entering/exiting coaches and face assault,” pointed out activist Nitin Gaikwad, who wrote to the Railways as recently as July demanding deployment of uniformed RPF personnel on platforms outside Divyangjan coaches.On March 27, a disabled commuter, identified only as Sajjad, was assaulted in a Karjat fast local by a woman and her minor son. Sajjad had questioned why she had entered a reserved coach when she did not have a disability. In May last year, a visually challenged woman was assaulted by a man after a row over seats on a Titwala-bound local.Gaikwad said altercations are more frequent at Thane, Ghatkopar and Dadar stations on CR.“Boarding the Divyangjan coach of a Kalyan, Titwala or Karjat-bound local train from these stations during evening peak hour is a daunting task,” he said. On WR, getting into a Virar local from Andheri and Borivli stations is a challenge.Some of the able-bodied travellers comprise policemen dressed in civvies. Activists had complained to the police department in the past, following which instructions were given to police personnel to stop travelling in reserved coaches. Activist Samir Zaveri, who has a 90% disability, said Railways must treat Thursday’s murder case as a wake-up call, ensure prompt action against violators, and take immediate steps to protect vulnerable passengers.The new Jan Vishwas Act imposes a severe penalty of Rs 2,000 for unauthorised travel in Divyangjan coaches. Under this law, RPF ( Western Railway ) prosecuted 524 people and penalised them Rs 10.48 lakh so far this year.“The fines collected under the Jan Vishwas Act this year are higher than penalties charged from nearly 4,800 offenders prosecuted under the Indian Railways Act,” said a WR official.
Article Summary: In 2025, the Railway Protection Force registered over 23,000 cases of unauthorised travel on Western and Central Railway put together. Disabled commuters continue to grapple with challenges while boarding and alighting from Divyangjan coaches that are packed with able-bodied passengers in peak hours.

Article Title: Co-passengers had offered a seat during row in Divyangjan coach in Mumbai local: Murder witness
Article Text:
Cajetan Pires, an amputee, was pushed off a moving local train by an able bodied passenger and killed

Mumbai:





An eyewitness to Thursday’s incident where a disabled commuter was pushed off a moving local train and killed by an able-bodied traveller following a row over seats told the police that onlookers had intervened and offered to make space, but to no avail. Police probe has also shown that the accused, Amjad Shaikh, was travelling without a ticket. Shaikh was produced before a railway magistrate court on Friday and was remanded to police custody till Aug 27.The victim, Cajetan Pires, 63, had an amputation in the left leg. He had boarded the Divyangjan coach of a Borivli local from Mahim station on Thursday. Shaikh was travelling in the same coach illegally from Lower Parel. “My brother preferred a seat where he could place his stick next to him for support,” said Pires’ sister, Maria. “He asked Shaikh to vacate the seat, but Shaikh was rude to him. When an argument broke out, co-passengers intervened and offered to give up one of their seats. But Shaikh did not move,” she said. Pires’ family met the eyewitness to find out what transpired in the coach. Police have recorded statements of two witnesses so far and are putting together the sequence of events that led to the incident.“What business did an able-bodied traveller (Shaikh) have in the handicapped coach?,” said a grief stricken Maria. Her daughter, Ria, said the family wants the strictest possible punishment for Shaikh. “Had he given up his seat, my uncle would have been alive today,” said Ria. Pires used to live with his sister and her family at Santacruz East until he moved out six months ago. He worked at a paan stall owned by a friend. “He was very headstrong but cared a great deal for me and my children. He would worry if we did not return home on time in the evenings. We cannot accept that he is no more,” said Maria.A post-mortem examination conducted at the Cooper Hospital on Friday revealed head injuries. “The moment the police called us and said that my uncle was unconscious from falling off a train, our hearts sank. At the hospital, we learnt that he had passed away,” said Ria. Pires’ funeral will be carried out on Saturday.
Article Summary: Cajetan Pires, an amputee, was pushed off a moving local train by an able bodied passenger and killed. Police probe has shown that the accused, Amjad Shaikh, was travelling without a ticket. Shaikh was produced before a railway magistrate court on Friday and was remanded to police custody till Aug 27.
